title.en: Getting Started: Train, Mine, Cut and Sell

description.en: Follow the mining loop and recognize the return, cutting and selling controls.

intro.en: Follow the mining loop and recognize the return, cutting and selling controls.

body.en: The developer identifies anvils as the source of Power. The reviewed recording shows a training hall with progressively stronger stations and a PLAY control when the player stands on a station. Check the station requirement before moving up.

title.en: 1. Build Power at the training area

paragraphs.en: The developer identifies anvils as the source of Power. The reviewed recording shows a training hall with progressively stronger stations and a PLAY control when the player stands on a station. Check the station requirement before moving up.

Begin with a station you can use. Watch the Power counter while training, then return to the mine to test the next floor. Some stations display a Robux option alongside progression information; read the purchase prompt before confirming.

The reviewed training hall displays 5x, 10x, 15x, 50x, 100x and 200x station labels. Some show Index progress requirements such as 0/15 and a Robux option. These are visible station labels, not a verified table of Power gained per second. Check the book counter and the question or purchase prompt before choosing a station.

title.en: 2. Break a floor and collect a rock

paragraphs.en: Floor panels show a durability bar and the rock types available in that room. Use your equipped pickaxe on the floor and watch the bar decrease. Once the room is accessible, approach a rock and use its interaction prompt.

In the recording the PC pickup prompt is E, and the blue bag counter changes when a rock is collected. A full bag limits the next collection trip. Use the current device prompt if it differs from the PC footage.

title.en: 3. Return home and load a cutting machine

paragraphs.en: Home (Q) appears at the top of the recorded PC interface, beside Spawn (F). At the machine, the prompt changes to Place Rock when it is available. Load a collected rock and let the cutting timer run.
A machine that is still cutting shows a countdown. A completed machine shows Ready! with an interaction prompt. Collect its result before trying to start the next cycle.

title.en: 4. Sell materials and choose the next upgrade

paragraphs.en: The home area has separate PICKAXE, UPGRADE and SELL stalls. The developer confirms that selling finds funds machine upgrades. After collecting a cut result, visit SELL and inspect the current sale options.

The reviewed frame locates the stall but does not show every sale-menu choice. Check the item and proceeds before confirming. Use the upgrade guides to choose between faster processing, more carrying space and stronger mining equipment.

question.en: What should I do when my bag is full?

answer.en: Return home, load available cutters and collect finished materials. Once space is free, return to mining. Consider Pocket if repeated trips limit your progress.

question.en: Why is a machine not ready for another rock?

answer.en: A countdown means it is still cutting. Ready! means its result can be collected. Check the prompt and collect the previous result before loading again.

title.en: Rock Cutting Machines: Loading and Upgrading

description.en: Keep machines occupied, collect finished materials and read upgrade costs before spending.

intro.en: Keep machines occupied, collect finished materials and read upgrade costs before spending.

body.en: At home, use Place Rock to load an available machine, wait for Ready!, then collect the materials. Cutting... (Upgrade) identifies an active machine. Keep several machines working while you collect another batch.

paragraphs.en: Load a collected rock at a machine displaying Place Rock, as shown in the getting-started guide. Once cutting begins, the prompt changes to Cutting... (Upgrade), with the machine level and a remaining-seconds counter visible. The image below shows this active state.

Several machines can run at once. Fill available machines before another collection trip, then return to collect the Ready results. The 26s and 20s in this screenshot are remaining countdowns for this moment, so they cannot establish full processing times or a speed multiplier.
Ready! replaces the timer on a finished machine. Use the nearby interaction prompt and check for material notifications. The recording shows different machines finishing at different times.
Do not treat the rock rarity as a guarantee of one particular material. The footage establishes the processing interface, but it does not supply a complete material probability table.

The upgrade panel shows the current machine level, the next level and a cash price. One recorded example displays Level 3 moving to 4 for $160K. That is a dated observation, not a permanent price list.

Upgrade the machine you intend to use and recheck its level after purchase. If cash is insufficient, finish and sell another batch. The reviewed panel does not quantify every level’s speed improvement.

The panel also displays Uncommon, Rare and Elite rock icons at Level 3. Treat these as visible interface entries. A complete eligibility ladder and the next level’s accepted rocks require additional footage. The $160K example is a cash upgrade, and the screenshot does not establish a speed percentage.

title.en: What continues while you are away

paragraphs.en: The official description says players gain Power offline and machines keep cutting while they are away. This supports preparing a batch before leaving.
The current offline cap, storage limit and exact payout formula are unverified. On return, inspect the available results and the game’s own offline summary before estimating an hourly return.

body.en: The UPGRADE stall contains Pocket and Eyesight cards. Pocket explicitly advertises +1 slot in the reviewed panel. The bag counter visible in the recording later changes from a three-slot maximum to four.

paragraphs.en: The UPGRADE stall contains Pocket and Eyesight cards. Pocket explicitly advertises +1 slot in the reviewed panel. The bag counter visible in the recording later changes from a three-slot maximum to four.
Choose carrying space when repeated trips interrupt collection while machines remain available. Check the current cost on the Pocket card, buy once and verify the new bag maximum.

In the recorded panel, Pocket is labelled LEVEL 4, +1 slot and $1M. The screenshot does not establish whether LEVEL 4 names the current or offered level, so compare your bag counter before and after purchase. This price is a recorded example and can change.
The same panel labels the second upgrade Eyesight and advertises +1 sight. The recording does not establish its exact range, reveal rules or effect on rare-rock chances.
Read the current in-game explanation before spending on it. No verified evidence supports claiming that Eyesight increases luck or changes the displayed room probabilities.

The same recorded panel labels Eyesight LEVEL 4, +1 sight and $340K. Its help button is visible, but the explanation is closed. This supports the upgrade name and displayed price only. Its exact visibility distance and interaction with the Index remain unknown.
The developer says stronger pickaxes help reach deeper floors. A dedicated PICKAXE stall is visible beside the other home shops, and later footage shows a different equipped pickaxe.

When a floor takes too long, compare the next pickaxe with the tool you own, and inspect its price and requirements. A complete current stat ladder is unavailable, so this guide does not rank every pickaxe.

title.en: Floors, Rock Rarity and the Index

description.en: Read the room panel before farming a rarity and keep collection rewards separate from drop odds.

intro.en: Read the room panel before farming a rarity and keep collection rewards separate from drop odds.

body.en: Each reviewed floor panel lists its possible rock types and percentages below the durability bar. Room 5 shows Uncommon, Rare, Elite and Nova Prism entries. Other rooms show different distributions.

paragraphs.en: Each reviewed floor panel lists its possible rock types and percentages below the durability bar. Room 5 shows Uncommon, Rare, Elite and Nova Prism entries. Other rooms show different distributions.

Use the panel for the room you are actually farming. Do not apply one screenshot’s percentages to every floor or multiply them into a material drop chance. Rock availability and the material obtained by cutting are separate stages.

These are the percentages printed in the reviewed room panels. They total 100.1%, so do not normalize them or assume a verified random-roll formula. The footage does not settle rounding or whether Nova Prism uses a separate roll. The table describes rock availability in those rooms, not the materials produced by a cutter.

rows.en: Recorded room panel; Rare label partially obscured

paragraphs.en: Deeper panels in the recording have substantially larger durability totals and different rock selections. The best practical target is a room you can break and refill from reliably with your current equipment.
If progress stalls at a floor, return to Power training, inspect pickaxe requirements and keep existing machines working. The exact best room depends on current equipment and the material you want.

Room 5 displays a total floor durability of 6.41M in the reviewed frame. Room 7 shows a much larger bar, but the player obscures part of its total, so no exact Room 7 durability is transcribed. Compare the visible bar with your actual damage and collection turnaround before committing to a deeper room.

title.en: Check Index rewards as your collection grows

paragraphs.en: The official description links Index completion with aura unlocks. An INDEX button is visible on the left of the gameplay interface. Open it to inspect the entries and requirements currently available to your account.
The reviewed frames do not show the full Index or aura effects. Exact completion thresholds, stacking rules and a best-aura ranking remain unverified.

question.en: Does Eyesight improve Nova Prism odds?

answer.en: The reviewed footage does not establish that effect. Eyesight advertises +1 sight, while room panels list rock percentages. Its exact function still needs the open help panel or a developer explanation.
